items.description: The text never states the domain size; it is shown only in Fig. 1. It can be worked out from Sec. 2 (level 2 = 80×40 grid with h2 = 0.25) and Remark 1 (320×160 cells), assuming '80×40' means cells along x × cells along y.
readings: L × H = 20 × 10, beam axis horizontal (aspect 2:1)
10 (x) × 20 (y), if '80×40' is read as rows × columns (unlikely for a cantilever)

items.description: Which boundary is supported, and over what length, is shown only in Fig. 1. The text says only 'cantilever' and mentions 'the Dirichlet boundary condition' (Sec. 3.5). The symmetric designs noted in Sec. 3.4 suggest a support that is symmetric about mid-height.
readings: entire left edge, x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H
central part of the left edge only (e.g. 0.25H–0.75H)
two short segments at the top and bottom left corners

items.description: The text never says which displacement components are fixed (Fig. 1 only; Sec. 3.5 just says 'Dirichlet boundary condition').
readings: fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 on the supported boundary
roller u_x = 0 along the edge plus u_y = 0 at a single point (mid-height)

items.description: The load location appears only in Fig. 1. Sec. 2 says all tests use this setup. Sec. 3.4 colour-codes only the bottom half 'exploiting the symmetry of the designs', which implies the load sits at mid-height of the free edge. The other common cantilever convention puts the load at a corner.
readings: right (free) edge at mid-height, x = L, y = 0.5H
right edge at the bottom corner, y = 0 (or mirrored top corner); conflicts with the symmetry remark

items.description: Eq. (1) writes compliance as ∫∂B u·t0 dA, i.e. a surface traction, but the length and profile of the loaded patch are never given (Fig. 1 only). A true point load would also make the compliance depend on the mesh under adaptive refinement.
readings: concentrated point load at the mid-height node
uniform traction on a centred segment of length h2 = 0.25 (0.025H)
uniform traction on a centred segment of length h0 = 1 (0.1H)
uniform shear traction over the whole right edge

items.description: The direction is given only in Fig. 1; a cantilever benchmark implies a transverse (vertical) load. In linear elasticity, flipping the load sign does not change the compliance, so up and down give the same layout and the same value.
readings: vertical, −y (downward)
vertical, +y (upward)

items.description: No force or traction magnitude is given anywhere (Sec. 2, Table 1). The reported compliances (~7.6e-5 with E = 1) imply a load far below unity, but the exact value cannot be recovered.
readings: unit total force F = 1
total force ≈ 1e-3 (rough estimate), calibrated so that plain VTTO gives F_c ≈ 7.61e-5 with E = 1 and unit thickness
unit traction t0 = 1 on the loaded segment (total force = segment length)

items.description: The text never says whether there are passive regions, e.g. a solid pad under the loaded patch or along the support. Only Fig. 1 could show them.
readings: none: the whole rectangle is designable
small solid (ρ = 1) non-design pad around the load application patch

items.description: Table 1 lists 'E 1, μ 0.3'. μ usually means the Lamé shear modulus, but this is almost certainly Poisson's ratio. Taken literally as a shear modulus with E = 1, it gives ν = E/(2μ) − 1 ≈ 0.67, which is not admissible for an isotropic material.
readings: Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
shear modulus μ = 0.3 (implies ν ≈ 0.67; physically implausible)

items.description: The text never says plane stress or plane strain. Sec. 2 treats ρ as out-of-plane sheet thickness, which implies plane stress. However, many 2D elasticity codes (e.g. deal.II examples) default to plane strain, which changes the effective ν to ν/(1−ν) ≈ 0.43.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.entity: out-of-plane thickness of a solid sheet (ρ = 1)
items.description: Sec. 2 reads ρ as out-of-plane thickness, but the thickness at ρ = 1 is not given. It multiplies the stiffness, so it scales the reported compliance values.
readings: t = 1 at ρ = 1
other reference thickness t (compliance scales as 1/t)

items.entity: standard SIMP reference run compared in Fig. 2
items.description: Sec. 2 and Fig. 2 compare VTTO with 'standard SIMP-based TO' (+17.2% compliance) but give no penalty exponent, continuation or projection for that run. p = 3 only appears later (Sec. 3.1), for low-thickness suppression.
readings: p = 3 fixed from the start, same PDE filter, no projection
p raised from 1 to 3 by continuation (rate unspecified), same filter
p = 3 plus a smoothed Heaviside projection

items.description: Table 1 gives the PDE filter 'Radius 0.375 (1.5h2)' but does not say whether this is the Helmholtz length parameter or the equivalent density-filter radius R. In Lazarov & Sigmund's convention r_PDE = R/(2√3), so the two readings differ by about 3.5× in length scale. A solver that only has a convolution filter also needs an equivalent value.
readings: PDE length parameter r = 0.375 in −r²∇²ρ̃ + ρ̃ = ρ
0.375 is the equivalent cone radius R, so r_PDE = 0.375/(2√3) ≈ 0.108
classical linear-hat density filter with R = 0.375 (6 cells at h = 0.0625)

items.description: The boundary conditions of the Helmholtz filter equation are not stated. They control how densities blur next to the clamped edge, the loaded patch and the free edges (Sec. 3.5 discusses edges near the Dirichlet boundary).
readings: homogeneous Neumann (the standard choice in Lazarov & Sigmund 2011)
zero-density Dirichlet / void padding outside the domain

items.description: Table 1 gives GOCM (Kim et al. 2021) with 'initial step length 0.05, decay 0.98 per iteration, min. 1e-4, design update exponential'. This paper never defines 'step length' or the 'exponential' update. If the step length is a move limit, it hits 1e-4 after about 308 iterations and effectively freezes the design. Plain VTTO (p = 1, linear filter) is convex, so a different optimizer should give nearly the same design only if it is run to convergence.
readings: step length = move limit on |Δρ_e| (0.05·0.98^k, floor 1e-4) with a multiplicative/exponential OC-type update
step length = step size of an exponential Lagrange-multiplier update, with a separate move limit
replace with standard OC (bisection) or MMA, run to convergence

items.description: Eq. (2) does not say whether Δρ_e is an absolute change (a signed sum would be about zero under an active volume constraint), or whether it uses raw or filtered densities. No maximum iteration count is given.
readings: volume-weighted mean of |Δρ_e| of raw design variables < 1e-4
same, but using filtered (physical) densities
either of the above, plus an iteration cap or a stop once the step length reaches its floor

items.description: The reported results use adaptive refinement: start at level 2 (80×40, h = 0.25), refine where the density jump > 0.05, coarsen where < 0.001, levels 0–4. The adaptation frequency, the density field used for the jump, and hanging-node handling are left to other papers. Remark 1 says a fixed 320×160 grid gives 'the same resolution', but the adaptive runs also use coarse h0 = 1 cells in void regions.
readings: uniform 320×160 grid, h = 0.0625 (Remark 1)
uniform 80×40 grid, h = 0.25 (initial level 2)
emulate the adaptive levels 0–4 with the jump criteria, adapting every iteration or every k iterations

items.description: Sec. 2 states h4 = 1·0.5^4 = 0.06125, but 0.5^4 = 0.0625. Only 0.0625 divides the 20×10 domain into the 320×160 grid of Remark 1.
readings: h4 = 0.06125 as printed

items.description: The finite element type of the deal.II implementation is not stated. Neither is how the PDE-filtered field is mapped back to element densities.
readings: bilinear 4-node Q1 quadrilaterals with element-wise constant density
higher-order (e.g. Q2) quadrilaterals

items.entity: reference compliance values in the Fig. 2 caption
items.description: The Fig. 2 caption gives 'SIMP-based TO and VTTO … 7.61e-5 and 8.92e-5, respectively', which would make VTTO the less stiff design. That contradicts the stated +17.2% from penalization, the Sec. 4.3 reference value of 7.62813e-5 (VTTO with low-thickness suppression) and the 0.26% increase in Fig. 3. This matters if the values are used to check the re-run or to calibrate the missing load.
readings: VTTO F_c = 7.61e-5, SIMP F_c = 8.92e-5 (consistent with the text)
SIMP F_c = 7.61e-5, VTTO F_c = 8.92e-5 (literal caption order)
